info.title: NASA EONET over Airnode
info.description:
NASA's Earth Observatory Natural Event Tracker: wildfires, volcanoes, severe storms, floods, droughts, dust events and sea and lake ice, curated in near real time from the agencies that observe them. This Airnode wraps it, so a consumer receives what EONET was tracking at a moment with a signature saying this Airnode read it then, which is what an event feed needs: whether something was burning is a question about a time.

An event is a thing happening somewhere, with a list of positions rather than one. A wildfire's list is its growth, a storm's is its track, and each entry carries the date it was observed and, where the observing agency published one, a magnitude in that magnitude's own unit. An event stays open until EONET closes it, and closed carries the date that happened.

EONET curates rather than observes. Every event names the source that reported it and links to that source's own record, which is where a consumer goes for the detail EONET does not carry. This Airnode serves the events and that link, and deliberately not EONET's imagery layers, since the imagery is somebody else's under terms of its own.

Data source: NASA Earth Observatory Natural Event Tracker (https://eonet.gsfc.nasa.gov). NASA produced material is generally free of copyright and reusable, including commercially, with attribution expected and no endorsement implied: NASA does not endorse, and is not affiliated with, API3, AirnodeHub or this Airnode.

Every response carries an EIP-191 signature from the Airnode that served it, so the data can be attributed back to its source rather than trusted on reputation.

oneOf.title: getEvents
oneOf.description: The natural events EONET is tracking, filtered.

operation.description:
Open events by default, which is the useful default and also the surprising one: asking for wildfires and getting nothing back means nothing is burning that EONET has open, not that the filter was wrong. Pass status to reach closed events or both. Every filter here narrows, and several combined narrow together, so a query that returns nothing is usually one filter too many rather than an error.

One combination is worth avoiding. Asking for every status with nothing else set is the whole archive back to the 1990s, which is tens of megabytes and most of a minute upstream before any of it is signed. Anything that bounds it, a limit, a days, a date range or a bounding box, takes that back to a normal call.

category.description: Only events in these categories, comma separated by id. Several are an or rather than an and. The categories operation lists the ids.

source.description: Only events reported by these sources, comma separated by id. Several are an or. The sources operation lists the ids.

status.description: Which events to include: open for what is still happening, closed for what has ended, all for both. Sending all with nothing else set returns the whole archive back to the 1990s, tens of megabytes, so bound it with limit, days, start and end, or bbox.

limit.description: How many events to return, most recently updated first.

days.description: Only events with an observation in this many prior days, today included.

start.description: First day of a range, inclusive. Paired with end.

end.description: Last day of a range, inclusive.

magID.description: Only events measured in this magnitude: ac for acres burned, mag_kts for wind speed. The magnitudes operation lists the ids, and this is what makes magMin and magMax mean anything, since a number is meaningless without its unit.

magMin.description: Only events at or above this magnitude, in the unit magID names.

magMax.description: Only events at or below this magnitude, in the unit magID names.

bbox.description: Only events inside this box, as four comma separated degrees in the order west,north,east,south. That example is the contiguous United States.

responseProjection.description: Optional. Maps a name of your choosing to an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the upstream response, such as {"price": "/ethereum/usd"}. data is then the text of a JSON object of those names in Unicode code point order, each value as the upstream wrote it, instead of the whole body, and the projection is part of the signed request identity. No two names take the same pointer, and no pointer is inside another's value. A pointer the response does not have is a 400.

operation.description: The same event the list returns, on its own, which is what a consumer holding an id from an earlier attestation asks for to see whether it has moved or closed since. An id that does not exist is refused.

id.description: The event, as EONET ids them.

responseProjection.description: Optional. oneOf.title: getMagnitudes
oneOf.description: The units an event can be measured in.

operation.description: Acres and hectares for a fire, knots for a storm's winds, and the seismic scales for a quake. Each carries the id the events operation's magID filter takes, and reading this is what turns a bare magnitudeValue on an event into a number with a unit on it.

Maps a name of your choosing to an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the upstream response, such as {"price": "/ethereum/usd"}. data is then the text of a JSON object of those names in Unicode code point order, each value as the upstream wrote it, instead of the whole body, and the projection is part of the signed request identity. 200.description: The upstream response and the attestation over it.

400.description: The operation exists but the parameters or the projection are missing, unknown or malformed, a path parameter is empty, . or .. or has such a part between slashes, or the projection names too many fields, an empty or repeated pointer, or a path the response does not have. Also a PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header that does not decode to a payment payload.

402.description: The operation is paid and no valid payment was supplied. The PAYMENT-REQUIRED header carries the x402 payment requirements to retry against.

502.description: The upstream API could not be reached or refused the request.

airnode.description: The address whose signature attests to this response.

requestHash.description: Identifies the request this response answers.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds at which the response was signed.

data.description: The upstream response body exactly as received, less a leading byte order mark. With a projection, the text of a JSON object keyed by the names it asked for in Unicode code point order, each value as the upstream wrote it.

attestation.digest: keccak256(abi.encodePacked(bytes32 requestHash, uint256 timestamp, bytes dataBytes))
attestation.requestHash: keccak256(utf8(JSON.stringify([operation, parameterEntriesSortedByName]))), where an object value is itself entries sorted by name, at any depth, and an array keeps its order. Names are compared by Unicode code point. A request that carries a projection appends its entries, sorted the same way, as a third element
attestation.verify: Recover the signer of the signature over the digest and check it equals the address above.

parameters.x-airnode-sign: false skips the signature: no attestation headers, and the body streamed through with no size cap.
parameters.x-airnode-project: alias:pointer, once per field to keep and at most 20 times, each pointer an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the upstream response that starts with /, is not repeated and is not inside another's value. The body becomes an object of those aliases in Unicode code point order, the signature covers it, and a pointer the response does not have is a 400.

passthrough.flow: Send the request the provider documents, method, path, query and body as they are, to url followed by the route's path. The body comes back as the upstream sent it, with the upstream's status, and on success the attestation is in the X-Airnode-Address, X-Airnode-Request-Hash, X-Airnode-Timestamp and X-Airnode-Signature headers, with the operation served in X-Airnode-Operation. Every query parameter starting with x-airnode- is this Airnode's own, listed under parameters, and never reaches the upstream.
passthrough.requestHash: keccak256(utf8(JSON.stringify(["passthrough", method, path, queryEntries, headerEntries, body]))), where method is upper case, path is what was sent after url as a URL parser resolves it, the query entries are what was sent with the Airnode's own parameters removed, in the order sent, headerEntries are the headers that the routes declare as parameters and the request sent, each name in lower case and sorted by Unicode code point, with the values of a header sent more than once joined with ", " in the order sent and the result trimmed of spaces and tabs, and body is the request body as sent, or an empty string. A request that carries a projection appends its entries, sorted by name in Unicode code point order, as a seventh element
passthrough.dataBytes: UTF-8 of the response body exactly as received, less a leading byte order mark, or of the projected object

payment.flow: An unpaid call to a priced operation returns 402 with the x402 payment requirements, base64-encoded, in the PAYMENT-REQUIRED header. Sign an EIP-3009 authorization matching one entry and retry the call with the payment payload, base64-encoded, in the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header. The settlement receipt comes back in the PAYMENT-RESPONSE header.
